{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Verify premises
premises_to_check = {
    'channels_exist': set(df['channel'].unique()) == {'email', 'paid_search'},
    'loyal_exists': 'loyal' in df['customer_segment'].unique(),
    'completed_status': set(df['status'].unique()) == {'completed', 'refunded'},
    'revenue_with_commas': df['revenue'].str.contains(',', na=False).any(),
    'qa_orders_present': (df['revenue'] == '999,999.99').sum() == 6
}

# Print results
for key, value in premises_to_check.items():
    print(f'{key}: {value}')

# The premise 'revenue_with_commas' is TRUE — the data does contain commas
# Even though sample values don't, full data does
# So the parsing step (strip commas) is needed

# Now parse revenue: strip commas and convert to float
df['revenue_numeric'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Filter out QA rows
df_clean = df[df['revenue_numeric'] != 999999.99]

# Filter for loyal, completed orders
df_loyal_completed = df_clean[
    (df_clean['customer_segment'] == 'loyal') & 
    (df_clean['status'] == 'completed')
]

# Compute mean revenue
mean_revenue = df_loyal_completed['revenue_numeric'].mean()
count_loyal_completed = len(df_loyal_completed)

print(f'Number of loyal, completed orders (after QA removal): {count_loyal_completed}')
print(f'Mean revenue: {mean_revenue:.2f}')"}
